body.x: JeiKei (CEO JaeGwan Kang) announced its participation in CES 2025 from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas. The company will present its innovative waste monitoring system, Watchman, at the K-Startup Pavilion.

Founded by faculty from Kyungnam University, JeiKei aims to tackle waste management issues near university neighborhoods in collaboration with Changwon City. The Watchman system, co-developed by JeiKei and local community centers, has significantly reduced waste since its pilot installation. Following its success, the system was commercialized with support from Changwon City and deployed across several areas, including Wolyeong-dong and Hapseong-dong.

JeiKei leverages innovative ideas and advanced technologies from academic research to address societal issues while developing reliable systems. The company is committed to protecting and preserving clean environments to enhance the quality of life for all.

At CES 2025, JeiKei will showcase its Watchman system to an international audience. The system includes two models: an AI-based model and a sensor-based model. The AI model employs deep-learning algorithms to detect and recognize waste-dumping activities accurately, enabling precise and intelligent monitoring.
The sensor-based model is designed as an eco-friendly monitoring system. It uses lightweight sensors that consume minimal energy and utilize solar power for sustainable operation.

JeiKei developed these models to deliver reliable performance and functionality. The company provides tailored solutions to address environmental challenges efficiently, aiming to expand its presence in the global market by catering to diverse customer needs.

A JeiKei representative stated, “At CES 2025, we plan to showcase our Watchman system’s innovative capabilities and reliability to international buyers and tech experts. We aim to create new market opportunities in regions facing waste management challenges by highlighting our successful implementations in local communities.”

The representative added, “We are also focusing on designing and developing a mobile version of the Watchman system to overcome the limitations of fixed installations. This will significantly enhance flexibility and convenience while improving recognition capabilities, enabling us to meet the needs of various monitoring environments.”
